schema: app | feature | currentRoute | standardDestination | liquidDestination | keyboardRoute | dataStateOwner | automatedProof | visualProof | status
rule: A row closes on an observed side effect, never on a control's presence. `observed` carries the literal before/after measurement; a row with no `observed` is explicitly not proven.

statusVocabulary.standard-only: deliberately never going Liquid; reason required inline
statusVocabulary.both: verified in standard and Liquid, each by side effect
statusVocabulary.REGRESSION: reachable in one and not the other; blocks the wave

rows.feature: Look up a word against the active dictionary source
rows.keyboardRoute: input is focusable and accepts real keystrokes; a synthetic Enter keydown did NOT trigger a search, so the keyboard route is UNPROVEN, not absent
rows.dataStateOwner: local JMdict via the main-process dictionary DB
rows.observed: typed 食べる, clicked Search: window went 38 -> 340 DOM nodes and 251 -> 2,926 chars; rendered 食べる/たべる, COMMON, #16403, PITCH, EN + RU glosses, 'JMdict (Japanese–English)'

rows.feature: Switch dictionary source by language (JA / ZH)
rows.observed: attribution text changed 'powered by Jisho (JMdict)' -> 'powered by CC-CEDICT'; content 2,926 -> 514 chars, rendering 食 shí and 食 sì; toggling back returned to 2,926 chars and the JMdict attribution EXACTLY — a verified reversible round trip

Interlinear: 2,926 -> 1,428 chars, adds 'Detected scale: word', 'Explain in Agent', and the provenance line 'The interlinear above is sourced from your dictionaries. The Agent explanation is AI-generated and uses its current provider, privacy, language…'. Returning to Dictionary mode restored 2,926 chars exactly

rows.feature: Per-result actions: play audio, copy to clipboard history, save to Flashcards, mark New, add to Anki
rows.currentRoute: Dictionary window > per-result controls (`Play 食べる`, `Copy to clipboard history`, `Save to Flashcards`, `食べる: New. Click to mark…`, `+ Add to Anki`)
rows.standardDestination: Flashcards store / Anki collection / clipboard history
rows.observed: the save control is stateful and reflects real stored state: two of three results render 'Saved to Flashcards' and the third renders 'Save to Flashcards'. NOT DRIVEN — these write to the user's collections; the wave that owns Dictionary must drive them with a reversible target

rows.currentRoute: Dictionary window > `Save search` (appears in the Saved searches header)
rows.standardDestination: saved-search list in the same window
rows.observed: `Save search` is ABSENT from the empty surface and PRESENT after a query completes — the control is query-conditional, not static chrome. Not driven: it persists user state

rows.standardDestination: notes list in the same window
rows.observed: pane and filter render on the empty surface; the list was empty on this profile so filtering has no observable effect to measure here

rows.feature: Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close
rows.standardDestination: in-desk floating window, or a real OS window when popped out
rows._note: pending here still means no Liquid destination; the standard half of every dictionary row above is driven and observed.
rows.observed: pop out created a SECOND real BrowserWindow at 900×640 (`/health` went 1 -> 2 windows, url `?popout=dictionary`) and removed the in-desk `.fwin`. The popped window rendered the app's INITIAL state — the active 食べる search did not carry across. Closing the popped window left NEITHER window: the desk returned to Scraper+Anki with no Dictionary. L3's reversibility requirement has to decide whether that last part is intended

rows.dataStateOwner: adopted Seanime library + directstream; the row comes from the study orchestrator document

BEFORE 27d584a8 the same click left the pane at `display:none` while the clip played unmuted at volume 1.0, currentTime 315 -> 359.96 s unattended — reproduced twice

rows.feature: Segment navigation (Library / Readiness / Review) without losing the player
rows.standardDestination: one pane shown, the library pane hidden but never unmounted
rows.keyboardRoute: three real buttons carrying aria-pressed; keyboard activation NOT driven
rows.dataStateOwner: MediaWorkspaceHost `view` state; the sidecar websocket lives in the library pane
rows.automatedProof: mediaWorkspaceHostReview.test.ts 'keeps the library pane MOUNTED but hidden'
rows.observed: Library -> Readiness hid the pane (computed `display:none`) with its 559 controls still mounted and the video element still present, paused at t=395.878722; returning to Library restored box 1264x821 at t=395.878722 EXACTLY, still paused — a byte-identical round trip, which is the reversibility L3 requires

rows.feature: Readiness category filters over the whole library
rows.currentRoute: Media workspace > Readiness > `Needs work` | `Not analysed` | `Out of date` | `No Japanese subtitles` | `Not imported` | `Ready`
rows.standardDestination: the same list, narrowed in place
rows.keyboardRoute: six real buttons; not driven by keyboard
rows.dataStateOwner: study orchestrator document joined to the adopted library
rows.observed: clicking `Ready 1` narrowed the pane from 138 buttons to 14, leaving exactly one row — THE Big O Episode 1 · N1 · 0% known · 1 card mined, 'Ready — Nothing to do — open it and study.' Header states '77 files · 76 need work · 1 ready to study' and 'Anki is connected · 84 decks'. The counts are honest: 76+1 = 77, and the one Ready row is the one that opens

At t=395.878 the highlighted row was 6:35 過去の歴史など無くとも文化とやらは装える with furigana beneath and the Russian subtitle line rendered over the canvas; the card preview names 'Cue 72 · track 0 · 395,617-398,083 ms', which matches the video clock rather than restating it

notWritten.reason: §5.3 says the ledger is created per app BEFORE that app is redesigned. Dictionary is written here because it is one of L1's two representative apps and because a ledger no one has driven is a template, not a ledger.
apps: mediaWorkspace — FOUR rows are now written and driven (2026-08-17, L4.2). What of §6.4 is still NOT driven, stated so no one reads four rows as the inventory: speed, volume, fullscreen, frame stepping, subtitle track/version choice, dual subtitles, offset and styling, transcript search/jump, dictionary/grammar/AI handoff, the mining write path itself, shadowing/dictation, block library reorder/detach, multi-monitor placement, and every degraded state. The mining and asset rows write to the user's collection, so they need a reversible target chosen before they are driven, not a click.
